indicator_definition: This indicator measures the share of energy from renewable sources (wind, solar, hydro, geothermal, ocean, biomass and biofuels) in gross final energy consumption, expressed as a percentage. It covers renewable energy used in electricity, heating and cooling, and transport. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy statistics.
rationale: Increasing the share of renewable energy is essential for reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the energy sector and achieving climate targets. Renewables also contribute to energy security and long-term cost reductions. Progress means a sustained increase in the renewable energy share in total energy consumption.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy statistics reported under Directive 2009/28/EC (Renewable Energy Directive) and its successor Directive 2018/2001/EU. Gross final energy consumption includes energy delivered to end users plus grid losses in electricity and distribution losses in heat networks.
indicator_name: Share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption
